decisions.rationale: Verified at 02be5a14 by parsing the bank with authoring/tools/gift/validate.mjs parseGift and comparing option answer lengths (correct vs longest distractor): 'o1 child first' 59 vs 44; 'o3 which program reads it' 92 vs 46 (the cue C2E-SEED-07 already reported, now back with the restored bank); also 'o3 server-side path' 41 vs 40 (a negligible margin). Is the remedy available on this branch? No. In authoring/tests/gift-answer-order.test.mjs, the test 'topic GIFT banks keep the semantics they had before the answer-order permutation' parses each bank at baseline f2647727 (present in this clone, so the test is not skipped). For every baseline question, baselineProblems() reports '<title> changed' when semanticDigest differs. In authoring/tools/gift/answer-order.mjs, semanticDigest hashes the category, the title, the stem and each option's [correct, answer, feedback] text. So any wording change that lengthens a distractor or trims a correct option changes the digest and fails npm test. This bank exists at the baseline. Its bytes at 02be5a14 are identical to origin/main (sha256 compared), so the length cue is pre-existing on main and not introduced by this branch's content. The only edit the test allows is appending new questions with new titles. That cannot remove the cue from the existing items, so it is not a fix. Decision: escalate, not reject, because the finding is true and fails C2 D7 ('the correct option is not the longest') and DESIGN.md Assessment. It cannot be accepted on this branch, because the only remedy needs a test or tooling change, which the branch may not make. The captain or tooling owner must decide whether to refresh the frozen baseline for reviewed wording-only length rebalancing, or to add a reviewed-exception mechanism. That would be a tooling branch, followed by a course or module branch that rebalances these items with answer-order.mjs, keeping each option's meaning and the keyed answer.
